supporting_docs: 4.2 Hollis Crane Engagement Letter - Matter 2291 Dawson.pdf
question_topics: Post-settlement legal fees or continuing obligations under the Dawson settlement
Confirmation that the insurer paid the Dawson settlement with no Company funding
Defense cost coverage and the $100,000 self-insured retention
Nature of the Dawson claim (customer property damage) and any similar claims
Post-close status of the Matter 1004 general corporate retainer
adjustments.rationale: Tied H&C 6400 activity to invoices. Matter 2291 (Dawson v. Meridian, a customer property-damage claim from a failed water heater) is five invoices totaling $84.5k in FY25, of which $30.0k (25-0910, 25-1120) falls in TTM. That portion is supportable as non-recurring: the case settled 11/14/25 and the CGL insurer funded the settlement. Defense costs sit within the $100k self-insured retention, so no reimbursement of the $84.5k is expected. Management's figure also sweeps in Matter 1004: the $2.5k/month general corporate retainer (2023 engagement letter, continuing until terminated by either party) and the Aug-25 employment policy review ($5.5k). Matter 1004 ran $36.0k in FY24 ($30.0k retainer plus $6.0k ad hoc), so it is part of the ongoing cost base and stays in EBITDA. Revised to the litigation invoices only.

question_topics: Basis for describing the Brightline managed-services fee as a one-time implementation cost
adjustments.rationale: Brightline bills $8.0k every month from Jan-25 for FieldPro managed services. Management's FY25 claim is all twelve invoices; its TTM 48,000 equals the Jul-Dec 2025 invoices, the claimed set under the tie-break. The MSA (signed Dec-24) is a 36-month managed service with a $8,000 monthly fee covering licensing, hosting and support, implementation included, renewing automatically. The controller's Mar-25 email calls it "our FieldPro subscription". This is the ongoing cost of the field service platform, which replaced the DispatchWorks license, not a one-time implementation. Reject.
